answer: Cross-epoch drift fingerprinting. Each identity accrues a vector of behavioural traces (timing, task mix, peer overlap) that must remain statistically stable across epochs. A sybil cluster’s copies drift apart or clone too tightly, both flagged like a karst sinkhole opening under a juniper grove. Enforcement: identities failing the consistency test lose routing priority and rewards for k epochs. Cost: an attacker must maintain N separate stable behavioural histories in parallel, multiplying operational effort per identity.
